blocks.text: North Delta Lots and Land: streets and boundaries

items.t: North Delta is the City of Delta's northern community, on the south bank of the Fraser River, north of Burns Bog and south of the river, with Scott Road (120 Street) as its eastern edge against Surrey.

Land here trades inside four board sub-areas — Annieville, Nordel, Scottsdale and Sunshine Hills Woods — with River Road and Annieville on the river side, Nordel at the Burns Bog edge, and the Scott Road corridor carrying the growth designations.
Delta's current Official Community Plan (OCP) is Bylaw No. 8400 (2024), one consolidated plan; North Delta's development permit areas (DPA = development permit area) sit in its Appendix B.

blocks.text: North Delta Lots and Land: the housing stock

items.t: North Delta lots are established fee-simple house lots — teardown, infill and resale parcels on serviced streets.

The Scott Road corridor is the exception to the house-lot pattern: the OCP's Scott Road Corridor designation supports apartment rezoning of house lots, as application LU009880 shows (lots zoned Single Detached Residential 1 (RS1), Duplex/Single Detached Residential 3 (RD3) and a comprehensive development zone proposed for Apartment Residential 6 (RA6)).

blocks.text: North Delta Lots and Land: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Three Appendix B permit areas shape North Delta lots: ND1 Fraser River Escarpment (the OCP lists mud flows, debris flows, erosion, land slip and subsidence on the river frontage), ND3 Annieville (the River Road village) and ND12 Nordel Social Heart (centred on 84 Avenue and 112 Street).

Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH = small-scale multi-unit housing) runs under Delta Bylaws 8394 and 8395, adopted June 24, 2024: suites, coach houses and garden suites are permitted in combination where the zoning applies — added units on an existing lot, not a subdivision right.
The west edge is protected, not developable: Burns Bog is held as the Burns Bog Ecological Conservancy Area by Metro Vancouver, and Delta Nature Reserve access is at 10388 Nordel Court.

blocks.text: North Delta Lots and Land: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Delta's 2026 flat-rate utility fee is $1,658 for a single-family home, covering garbage and recycling and, in the City's own words, water and sewer "where applicable" — so servicing on a specific vacant parcel is a City confirmation, not an assumption.
The earlier North Delta area plan was folded into the consolidated OCP, Bylaw No. 8400 (2024). City documents that predate July 2024 may still refer to it.

Delta's zoning bylaw number is contested on City sources (pages cite No. 7600, 2017; an internal title reads "8400, 2025," which is the OCP's number) — take the parcel's zone from the City's zoning maps for the address, never from a bylaw number quoted in a listing.
Tree removal on a Delta lot is governed by the Delta Tree Protection and Regulation Bylaw No. 7969, 2021, including replacement planting or cash in lieu.

blocks.text: North Delta Lots and Land: costs and taxes

items.t: The 2026 flat-rate utility fee is $1,658 for a single-family home; Delta bills flat-rate utilities in late February and metered homes quarterly.
The 2026 provincial school tax for School District No. 37 (Delta) is $1.0997 per $1,000 of residential value, set provincially.

blocks.text: North Delta Lots and Land: getting around

items.t: Highway 91 and the Alex Fraser Bridge are North Delta's freeway link to Richmond and Vancouver, and Highway 99 runs along its south side past Burns Bog; Scott Road (120 Street) is the Surrey boundary arterial and the corridor the OCP designates for growth.

blocks.text: North Delta Lots and Land: risks and due diligence

items.t: The ND1 Fraser River Escarpment permit area is the named hazard frame for river-side lots: the OCP lists mud flows, debris flows, erosion, land slip and subsidence there, and the permit-area map shows where the area applies — it does not certify any one lot safe, which needs a parcel-level geotechnical answer.
Burns Bog edge lots sit beside a protected peat bog conservancy: check development permit and environmental conditions early, because setback or covenant conditions surface late in deals.
Whether any specific North Delta parcel is in the Agricultural Land Reserve is a parcel check on the Agricultural Land Commission maps by PID or civic address; no North Delta ALR split is published.

faq.q: What did lots and land in North Delta sell for?
faq.a: From November 2025 to late October 2026, North Delta recorded 5 lot and land sales at a median of $1,125,000.

faq.q: How long do lots and land take to sell in North Delta?
faq.a: The median was 83 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 86.5% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Do lots and land in North Delta sell above asking price?
faq.a: 0% of the 5 lots and land sold for more than the last list price, and the median sale was 86.5% of it.

faq.q: Is North Delta a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026 houses in North Delta had a sales ratio of 20%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market, and condos and townhomes 9%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many lots and land are for sale in North Delta?
faq.a: The listing feed on this page shows what is active now, and the number changes daily. Ask Jared and he will send you the lots and land in North Delta that match what you want.

faq.q: Can Jared alert me when lots and land come up in North Delta?
faq.a: Yes. Tell him the area, price range and must-haves and he will alert you the day a match is listed.

faq.q: Where can I see all North Delta homes?
